passage:
A town kept an old factory whistle as a memorial. It once marked the beginning and end of workers' shifts.
At the yearly labor festival, the whistle was sounded once. Former workers stood quietly. Younger people covered their ears and laughed nervously.
A teacher explained to students that the sound once controlled daily life. People woke, ate, worked, and rested according to it.
The whistle was loud and not beautiful, but it was honest.
History is not always pleasant music. Sometimes it is a harsh sound that reminds people of labor, discipline, and the lives behind the products a town was built on.
